text:
Forgive me, dry leaf,

I cannot care for you.

I came to love in this world,

and even love I lost.

What use was weaving flowers

in the sands of the ground

if there were people sleeping

upon their own heart?


And I could not raise them up!

I weep for what I did not do

and for this weakness

that makes me sad and unhappy.

Forgive me, dry leaf!

My powerless eyes are

keeping watch and praying for those

who will not rise.


You are an autumn leaf

flying through the garden.

I leave you my nostalgia

—the best part of me.

And I go along this road,

sure of how useless everything is.

For everything is less than the wind,

less than the leaves on the ground.

translation.title: Autumn Song
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the dry-leaf apostrophe and the speaker's grief over failed love, failed aid, and uselessness.
